title: 8 Best All-Inclusive Family Resorts in Vietnam 2026
excerpt: Vietnam is the hottest family travel destination in Southeast Asia right now. We've hand-picked 8 all-inclusive resorts that deliver incredible value, amazing kids' clubs, and unforgettable experiences for the whole family.
author: Nudge Travel

content.introduction: Vietnam has quietly become one of Southeast Asia's most compelling family travel destinations. With its stunning coastline stretching over 3,000 kilometers, world-class hospitality, and prices that make other Asian beach destinations look expensive, it's no wonder families are flocking here. The all-inclusive resort scene has matured dramatically in the past few years, with international brands and local gems alike stepping up their family offerings. From the historic shores of Da Nang to the tropical paradise of Phu Quoc, here are the 8 best all-inclusive family resorts in Vietnam that will make your 2026 family vacation unforgettable.

sections.heading: Why Vietnam for Family Travel in 2026?
sections.body: Vietnam offers exceptional value for families. A five-star all-inclusive resort here costs roughly half of what you'd pay in Thailand or Bali for equivalent quality. The food is incredible, the people are genuinely warm toward children, and the variety of experiences — from pristine beaches to vibrant cities to limestone karst bays — means there's something for every type of family. Vietnam has also invested heavily in infrastructure. Da Nang's international airport now connects directly to most major Asian cities, Phu Quoc has a brand-new terminal, and the road between Hanoi and Ha Long Bay has been upgraded significantly. For families tired of the crowds in Phuket and Bali, Vietnam offers a more authentic, less commercialized alternative that doesn't sacrifice comfort.

sections.heading: What to Look for in a Family All-Inclusive Resort
sections.body: When choosing an all-inclusive resort for your family in Vietnam, consider these key factors. Kids' clubs should be staffed by trained professionals with structured daily programs — not just a room with toys. Look for resorts with multiple dining options so picky eaters always have something they enjoy. Pool complexes should have dedicated children's areas with shallow water and shade. Location matters too: resorts near international airports (Da Nang, Cam Ranh, Phu Quoc) mean less travel time after a long flight. Finally, check if the resort offers connecting rooms or family suites — Vietnamese resorts are increasingly catering to families with proper multi-room configurations rather than just adding a rollaway bed.

resorts.name: Vinpearl Resort & Spa Da Nang
resorts.description: Vinpearl Resort & Spa Da Nang is a sprawling beachfront complex set on the pristine Non Nuoc Beach, consistently ranked among the world's most beautiful beaches. This resort delivers extraordinary value for families with its massive free-form pool complex, dedicated kids' club with daily programs, and direct access to the VinWonders Da Nang amusement park — one of the largest in Southeast Asia. The resort's 800 meters of private beach are patrolled by lifeguards, giving parents genuine peace of mind. Rooms are spacious by Vietnamese standards, with family suites offering separate living areas and multiple bathrooms. The all-inclusive package covers buffet breakfast, lunch, and dinner at multiple restaurants serving Vietnamese, Japanese, Italian, and international cuisine, plus selected beverages throughout the day.
resorts.bestFor: Families who want an amusement-park-adjacent resort experience
highlights: Adjacent to VinWonders Da Nang — one of Asia's largest amusement parks
800m private beach with lifeguards
Massive free-form swimming pool with waterslides
Four on-site restaurants included in all-inclusive
Separate kids' pool and splash zone
EV charging stations available in the parking area
Babysitting service available for evening adult time

resorts.name: JW Marriott Phu Quoc Emerald Bay Resort & Spa
resorts.description: The JW Marriott Phu Quoc is not just a resort — it's a design masterpiece. Architect Bill Bensley created a whimsical 'university campus' theme complete with faux academic buildings, a grand quadrangle, and interiors that feel like a living art gallery. Located on the stunning Khem Beach (often called the most beautiful beach on Phu Quoc), this resort offers five swimming pools, an incredible kids' club with daily art and science workshops, and the award-winning Cham Spa for parents who need a proper break. The all-inclusive package is generous, covering meals at several of the resort's restaurants — including the French fine-dining venue and the casual beachfront grill. While it's the priciest option on this list, the level of service, attention to detail, and overall experience make it worth every dong for discerning families.
resorts.bestFor: Design-loving families who appreciate luxury and unique architecture
highlights: Bill Bensley-designed 'university campus' theme — Instagram heaven
Five swimming pools including an adults-only infinity pool
Kids' club with art, cooking, and science workshops
Khem Beach — consistently rated Phu Quoc's best beach
Cham Spa — one of Vietnam's top luxury spas
Multiple dining venues from street food to fine dining
Complimentary kayaking, paddleboarding, and snorkeling gear

resorts.name: Melia Ho Tram Beach Resort
resorts.description: Just a two-hour drive from Ho Chi Minh City, Melia Ho Tram Beach Resort offers city-weary families an escape without the hassle of a flight. Set on 20 hectares of tropical gardens along a stunning stretch of private beach, this Spanish-owned resort brings Mediterranean warmth to the Vietnamese coast. The kids' club is exceptional — staffed by trained childcare professionals with a full daily schedule of activities including cooking classes, beach games, arts and crafts, and even mini-golf. Parents will love the YHI Spa, the sprawling lagoon-style pool, and the fact that this is one of the few resorts in Vietnam with a proper EV charging station. The all-inclusive package includes buffet meals at the main restaurant plus selected alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverages. Rooms are contemporary and spacious, with the family connecting rooms offering exceptional value.
resorts.bestFor: Weekend getaways from Ho Chi Minh City
highlights: Only 2 hours from Ho Chi Minh City — no flight needed
20 hectares of tropical gardens with direct beach access
Lagoon-style pool stretching through the property
Daily kids' activities including mini-golf and cooking classes
YHI Spa with extensive treatment menu
EV charging station available
Excellent value compared to Saigon weekend alternatives

resorts.name: Premier Village Phu Quoc Resort
resorts.description: Premier Village Phu Quoc is the ideal choice for multi-generational family groups or families who want serious space. Every accommodation is a private villa with its own infinity pool — yes, your own pool. Villas range from two to five bedrooms, making this perfect for extended family reunions or two families traveling together. Located on the southwest coast of Phu Quoc near the famous Sunset Town, the resort offers sweeping ocean views and spectacular sunsets every evening. The kids' club runs a full program of Vietnamese cultural activities — lantern making, cooking classes, and traditional games — that give children a genuine cultural experience rather than just generic childcare. The all-inclusive package covers meals at the resort's restaurants plus in-villa dining options, making it easy for parents of young children to eat dinner without leaving the comfort of their villa.
resorts.bestFor: Extended family groups and multi-generational trips
highlights: Every villa has its own private infinity pool
Two to five-bedroom villas for large family groups
Located near Sunset Town with spectacular evening views
Cultural kids' club with Vietnamese lantern making and cooking
In-villa dining included in all-inclusive package
Access to Sunset Town's night market and shows
Complimentary bicycles and kayaks for guests

resorts.name: Fusion Resort Cam Ranh
resorts.description: Fusion Resort Cam Ranh turns the all-inclusive model on its head with its innovative 'All-Spa-Inclusive' concept — every guest receives complimentary spa treatments at the resort's award-winning spa. Yes, that means a free 60-minute spa treatment per person per day, included in your rate. This is a game-changer for parents who usually sacrifice self-care on family holidays. Located on Long Beach in Cam Ranh (just 20 minutes from Cam Ranh International Airport), the resort features two large pools, a private beach, and a kids' club with eco-focused activities like beach cleanups and gardening. The all-inclusive package covers meals at the resort's restaurants with an emphasis on fresh, locally-sourced ingredients. The beachfront villas with plunge pools are particularly popular with families who want privacy and direct beach access. The resort also offers complimentary yoga and meditation classes daily.
resorts.bestFor: Parents who want daily spa treatments without the guilt
highlights: All-Spa-Inclusive — free 60-min spa treatment per person daily
20 minutes from Cam Ranh International Airport
Eco-focused kids' club with beach cleanups and gardening
Premium beachfront villas with private plunge pools
Farm-to-table dining philosophy
Complimentary daily yoga and meditation classes
Two large pool complexes including a dedicated family pool

resorts.name: InterContinental Danang Sun Peninsula Resort
resorts.description: Perched on the lush Son Tra Peninsula overlooking the East Sea, the InterContinental Danang is widely regarded as Vietnam's most luxurious resort. Designed by the legendary Bill Bensley, the resort cascades down a hillside in four distinct tiers — Heaven, Sky, Earth, and Sea — connected by a funicular railway that kids absolutely adore. The resort's Planet Trekkers kids' club is one of the best in Asia, offering a full program of Vietnamese cultural activities, cooking classes, and outdoor adventures in the surrounding jungle. The all-inclusive package covers dining at the resort's three signature restaurants including Chef Michel Roux's stunning La Maison 1888. The private beach is immaculate, the three pools (including an adults-only infinity pool) are spectacular, and the HARNN Heritage Spa offers traditional Vietnamese treatments in a cave-like setting carved into the hillside.
resorts.bestFor: Luxury-seeking families who want a resort that feels like a destination
highlights: Bill Bensley design with funicular railway connecting four tiers
Planet Trekkers kids' club — one of Asia's best
La Maison 1888 — Michel Roux's fine dining restaurant
Private beach on the Son Tra Peninsula
HARNN Heritage Spa in a cave-like setting
Three swimming pools including adults-only infinity pool
Vietnam's only Forbes Five-Star resort

resorts.name: Mövenpick Resort Waverly Phu Quoc
resorts.description: Mövenpick Resort Waverly Phu Quoc brings Swiss precision to the tropical paradise of Phu Quoc. Located on the island's stunning southwest coast near the famous Sunset Town, this resort offers a perfect balance of luxury and family-friendly comfort. The highlight for families is the spectacular free-form swimming pool that winds through the property, complete with waterslides, a dedicated kids' pool, and plenty of shaded lounging areas for parents. The kids' club runs structured daily programs with art workshops, Vietnamese cooking classes, treasure hunts, and beach games — all supervised by multilingual staff. The all-inclusive package is comprehensive, covering meals at the resort's three restaurants plus afternoon tea (true to the Mövenpick tradition), selected beverages, and even ice cream for the kids. Spacious family rooms with ocean views and direct pool access make this a top choice for families who want convenience without sacrificing quality.
resorts.bestFor: Families who want Swiss hospitality in a tropical setting
highlights: Spectacular free-form pool with waterslides and kids' pool
Structured daily kids' activities with multilingual staff
Mövenpick afternoon tea tradition included
Complimentary ice cream for kids every afternoon
Direct pool access rooms available
Located near Sunset Town for evening exploration
Spacious family rooms with ocean views

resorts.name: Ana Mandara Cam Ranh
resorts.description: Ana Mandara Cam Ranh offers a refreshingly different take on the all-inclusive experience. Instead of a massive high-rise hotel, this resort is a collection of low-rise villas and rooms set within 11 hectares of tropical gardens on a pristine stretch of white sand beach. The vibe is relaxed and unpretentious — think barefoot luxury rather than formal elegance. The kids' club focuses on outdoor activities: sandcastle building, beach volleyball, traditional Vietnamese games, and nature walks through the resort's gardens. The all-inclusive package includes meals at the resort's main restaurant with a strong focus on fresh seafood and local Vietnamese cuisine, plus selected beverages. The real draw here is the setting: Long Beach in Cam Ranh is one of Vietnam's most beautiful and least crowded beaches, offering calm waters perfect for young children to swim in. The resort also offers complimentary non-motorized watersports including kayaking, stand-up paddleboarding, and sailing.
resorts.bestFor: Families who want a relaxed, unpretentious beach holiday
highlights: Low-rise villa-style accommodation in tropical gardens
Long Beach — one of Vietnam's calmest, cleanest beaches
Outdoor-focused kids' club with beach games and nature walks
Complimentary kayaking, paddleboarding, and sailing
Fresh seafood-focused dining included in all-inclusive
Peaceful setting away from crowds
Excellent value for a high-end beach resort

content.conclusion: Vietnam's all-inclusive resort scene has never been stronger, and 2026 is the perfect year to experience it with your family. Whether you choose the amusement-park thrills of Vinpearl Da Nang, the design-forward luxury of JW Marriott Phu Quoc, or the relaxed beach vibes of Ana Mandara Cam Ranh, you'll find exceptional value, warm hospitality, and unforgettable family memories awaiting you. For families planning their trip, the best strategy is to book early — especially for peak season travel between November and April, when Vietnam's southern resorts enjoy their best weather. Consider splitting your stay between two destinations if you have a longer trip: combine the cultural richness of Da Nang with the island paradise of Phu Quoc, or pair a few days in Ho Chi Minh City with a beach retreat at Melia Ho Tram. No matter what you choose, Vietnam's family-friendly hospitality will leave you planning your next visit before you've even checked out.

tips.tip: Best time to visit: November to April for southern resorts (Phu Quoc, Cam Ranh), February to August for central resorts (Da Nang, Hoi An).
Book all-inclusive packages directly through resort websites for the best rates and family add-ons.
Vietnam e-visas are available for most nationalities and take 3-5 business days to process.
Most resorts offer free airport transfers when you book the all-inclusive package — always ask before booking a taxi.
